SolutionLaTeX: \begin{aligned}\int\cot x\,dx&=\int\frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\,dx\\u&=\sin x,\quad du=\cos x\,dx\\\int\frac{1}{u}\,du&=\ln|u|+C\\\int\cot x\,dx&=\ln|\sin x|+C\end{aligned}
Explanation: Rewrite \(\cot x\) as \(\cos x/\sin x\). The numerator is the derivative of the denominator. Include the constant of integration. The antiderivative applies on intervals where \(\sin x\ne0\).

SolutionLaTeX: \begin{aligned}u&=\tan x,\quad u'=\sec^2 x\\\frac{d}{dx}e^u&=e^u u'\\\frac{d}{dx}e^{\tan x}&=e^{\tan x}\sec^2 x\end{aligned}
Explanation: Differentiate the exponential, then multiply by the derivative of its exponent.
The exponent decreases without bound. An exponential with base e approaches zero as its exponent approaches negative infinity.
The derivative gives the tangent slope at each x-value. No particular x-value is specified in the published problem, so the slope is given as a function of x.
